query: According to episode 7, why can no machine decide in general whether an arbitrary program halts?
answer: Turing shows that a “universal halt‑detector” can’t exist. If we suppose a machine (the *checker*) that, given any program and its input, always tells us whether that program will eventually stop, we can feed the checker its own description and then build a “troublemaker” that does the opposite of whatever answer the checker gives. When the troublemaker is run on its own description, the checker’s prediction must be wrong—whether it says “halts” or “runs forever” the troublemaker flips the outcome. Because this self‑referential construction leads to a contradiction, no consistent machine can decide halting for every possible program. Thus the halting problem is undecidable and there is no mechanical procedure that can answer it in general (Episode 7, 26:22‑27:51; 24:54‑26:21; 23:24‑24:54).
